title: Channel Islands Camera Traps
description: Camera trap photograph dataset from the Channel Islands, comprising approximately 240,000 JPEG images collected for wildlife monitoring. Suitable for ecological research and machine learning model development on island fauna.

# Channel Islands Camera Traps

### Channel Islands Camera Traps

#### S3 base

`s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/agentmorris/lila-wildlife/channel-islands-camera-traps`

#### Overview

This data set contains 246,529 camera trap images from 73 camera locations in the Channel Islands, California. All animals are annotated with bounding boxes. Data were provided by The Nature Conservancy.

Animals are classified as rodent1 (82914), fox (48150), bird (11099), skunk (1071), or other (159). 114,949 images (47%) are empty.

1All images of rats were taken on islands already known to have rat populations.

#### Citation, license, and contact information

If you use these data in a publication or report, please use the following citation:

The Nature Conservancy (2021): Channel Islands Camera Traps 1.0. The Nature Conservancy. Dataset.

For questions about this data set, contact [Nathaniel Rindlaub](mailto:nathaniel.rindlaub@TNC.ORG) at The Nature Conservancy.

This data set is released under the [Community Data License Agreement (permissive variant)](https://cdla.io/permissive-1-0/).

The original data set included a “human” class label; for privacy reasons, we have removed those images from this version of the data set. Those labels are still present in the metadata.

#### Data format

Annotations are provided in [COCO Camera Traps](https://github.com/agentmorris/MegaDetector/blob/main/megadetector/data_management/README.md#coco-camera-traps-format) format.

For information about mapping this dataset's categories to a common taxonomy, see [this page](https://lila.science/taxonomy-mapping-for-camera-trap-data-sets/).

#### Downloading the data

Metadata is available [here](https://storage.googleapis.com/public-datasets-lila/channel-islands-camera-traps/channel-islands-camera-traps.json.zip) (18MB).

Images are available as a single zipfile:

[Download from GCP](https://storage.googleapis.com/public-datasets-lila/channel-islands-camera-traps/channel-islands-camera-traps-images.zip) (86GB)  

[Download from AWS](http://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop.s3.amazonaws.com/agentmorris/lila-wildlife/channel-islands-camera-traps/channel-islands-camera-traps-images.zip) (86GB)  

[Download from Azure](https://lilawildlife.blob.core.windows.net/lila-wildlife/channel-islands-camera-traps/channel-islands-camera-traps-images.zip) (86GB)  

Images are also available (unzipped) in the following cloud storage folders:

* gs://public-datasets-lila/channel-islands-camera-traps/images (GCP)
* s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/agentmorris/lila-wildlife/channel-islands-camera-traps/images (AWS)
* https://lilawildlife.blob.core.windows.net/lila-wildlife/channel-islands-camera-traps/images (Azure)

We recommend downloading images (the whole folder, or a subset of the folder) using [gsutil](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/gsutil) (for GCP), [aws s3](https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/documentation/api/latest/reference/s3/index.html) (for AWS), or [AzCopy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-use-azcopy-v10) (for Azure). For more information about using gsutil, aws s3, or AzCopy, check out our [guidelines for accessing images without using giant zipfiles](http://lila.science/image-access).

Having trouble downloading? Check out our [FAQ](http://lila.science/faq#downloadtips).

#### Other useful links

[MegaDetector](https://github.com/agentmorris/MegaDetector/blob/main/megadetector.md) results for all camera trap datasets on LILA are available [here](https://lila.science/megadetector-results-for-camera-trap-datasets/).

Information about mapping camera trap datasets to a common taxonomy is available [here](https://lila.science/taxonomy-mapping-for-camera-trap-data-sets/).
